title: Supplier Technical Control Attestation Checklist and Evidence Matrix
content:
Purpose:
This working checklist is intended for use during vendor onboarding and periodic reassessment for suppliers that interact with inference workloads or customer data. It focuses on technical controls (network, keys, model artifacts, logs) and the minimum evidence our legal + security teams need to accept residual risk.

How to use this doc:
- Send the checklist to vendor (editable). Vendors should either: (1) return the attested answers with evidence links, or (2) provide timeboxed access (read-only) to relevant artifacts.
- Reviewer (security engineer) scores each item: pass / partial / fail and records evidence id(s).
- Negotiation notes and compensating controls go in the "reviewer comments" section.

Scoring & thresholds (recommended):
- Acceptable for low-risk suppliers: 80% pass, no critical fails.
- Acceptable for high-risk (any access to production model weights, raw customer PII, or on-prem integration): 95% pass, zero critical fails, required pen-test within last 12 months.

Checklist (attestations vendor must complete):
1) Identity & Access Management
   - Single sign-on enforced for all operator accounts (SAML/OIDC). Evidence: screenshot of IdP config or audit log export.
   - MFA required for all admin-level and remote access. Evidence: admin account policy or audit report.
   - Role-based access controls defined for model/system access, with least privilege enforcement. Evidence: RBAC matrix or IAM policy export.

2) Cryptography & Key Management
   - Data at rest encryption for model weights, logs, and backups (algorithm + key length). Evidence: storage config + KMS key ARN/policy.
   - Customer data encryption in transit (TLS 1.2+ with modern cipher suites). Evidence: TLS cert chain or scan.
   - KMS integration details (who manages keys, rotation schedule, HSM usage if any). Evidence: KMS policy and rotation logs.

3) Infrastructure & Network Controls
   - Network segmentation that separates model-training/experimental environments from production inference. Evidence: network diagrams + firewall rules.
   - Egress controls and data exfil prevention policies for inference nodes. Evidence: egress ACLs, WAF rules, or proxy configs.
   - Secure remote access (jump hosts, bastion + recorded sessions). Evidence: bastion audit logs or session recordings.

4) Model and Artifact Protections
   - Access controls for model weights and deployment artifacts (who can pull weights). Evidence: artifact repository ACL export.
   - Integrity checks (checksums, signed artifacts) for model weights and release binaries. Evidence: release process doc or signature verification records.
   - Versioning and rollback capabilities documented. Evidence: release notes or deployment pipeline.

5) Logging, Monitoring & Retention
   - Structured audit logs for admin actions, model loads, and inference requests (if applicable). Evidence: sample logs with redaction and retention policy.
   - Alerting and incident detection (SIEM integration, detection rules). Evidence: detection rule list or PagerDuty integration screenshot.
   - Log retention and deletion policy aligned with contracted retention terms. Evidence: retention settings and scheduled deletion job outputs.

6) Data Minimization & Processing Controls
   - Controls to avoid storing unnecessary input prompts or PII after inference (default redaction or ephemeral buffers). Evidence: code snippets, retention config.
   - Clear description of any training or reprocessing that could use customer data. Evidence: data flow docs, contracts.

7) Vulnerability Management & Penetration Testing
   - Recent vulnerability scanning cadence and coverage of inference hosts. Evidence: scan reports.
   - Penetration test within 12 months for high-risk vendors; remediation tracker for findings. Evidence: pen-test report + closure tickets.

8) Subprocessors & Third Parties
   - List of subprocessors with roles and locations. Evidence: subprocessors registry (latest export).
   - Contracts in place with subprocessors that mirror Redwood’s security obligations. Evidence: sample subprocessor contract clause or addendum.

9) Business Continuity & Backup
   - Backup frequency and recovery objectives for model artifacts and critical config. Evidence: backup schedule and restore test logs.
   - Disaster recovery plan and last DR exercise date. Evidence: DR runbook and postmortem notes.

10) Incident Response & Breach Notification
   - Incident response runbook that covers exfiltration of model weights and sensitive logs. Evidence: runbook excerpt.
   - Contractual SLA for incident notification to Redwood (72 hours for critical incidents). Evidence: signed contract clause or vendor attestation.

Evidence Matrix (what we expect to receive):
- Policy/diagram PDFs (network, retention, DR): required
- Configuration exports (IAM, KMS, ACLs): required for any systems storing customer data
- Redacted logs / sample audit log extracts: required (if vendor claims logging)
- Pen-test/vuln scan reports: required for high-risk vendors, preferred otherwise
- Screenshots of console configs are acceptable as interim evidence but must be accompanied by exports within 10 business days.

Reviewer checklist (internal):
- Map each vendor answer to Redwood control families (SOC2/ISO/PCI where applicable).
- Identify compensating controls for any partial/fail items and estimate residual risk.
- Escalate to legal for any deviation from standard notification or data handling terms.
- For any access to model weights or raw customer PII, require Dedicated review (eng + product).

Negotiation and fallback playbook (notes to SE / Legal):
- If vendor cannot provide KMS integration: require at-rest encryption with provider-supplied keys and quarterly key rotation proof.
- If vendor cannot do pen-test: require increased monitoring, mandatory log forwarding to Redwood (read-only) for 90 days, and a contractual right to audit.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Agree on an evidence id convention that maps to internal dtrack tickets (e.g., EVID-<vendor>-<item>).
- Define exact retention thresholds for non-production inference logs (product to confirm).
- Confirm whether we can accept third-party SOC2 + vendor-signed attestation for low-risk suppliers.

Appendix A: sample vendor response format
- Item id, vendor_answer (pass/partial/fail), evidence_links (publicly accessible or S3 presigned), comments, date_submitted.

Appendix B: quick links
- Confluence assessment template: https://confluence.redwoodinc/internal/security/vendor-assessments
- Current onboarding flow: JIRA-ONB-1089
- Slack thread for vendor exceptions: #sec-vendor-exceptions

Notes to self (Maya):
- Will spin up a short Google Form that maps to this checklist and auto-attaches to the vendor onboarding ticket.
- Follow up with Product (Aisha) on retention thresholds by 2026-03-15.

This is a living working doc — expect changes after first two vendor runs.
